statements.statement_en: Judges and lawyers should hold the majority on the committee that selects judges, even if elected officials have little say over who becomes a judge.
Yeshiva students should be drafted into the army or civilian service, even if this forces them to give up full-time Torah study.
Every citizen, including groups that are exempt today, should do compulsory military or civilian service, even if the army does not need all of them.
Israel should restrict more strictly the entry and residence of foreigners, including citizens' spouses who come from the Palestinian territories, even if this separates some families.
Israel should reduce the number of foreign workers, even if construction, agriculture and elderly care become more expensive.
Getting a divorce should be easier, even if one of the spouses objects.
Suspects and defendants should have fewer legal protections during arrest, questioning and trial, even if the risk of convicting innocent people grows.
More people should qualify for disability, nursing-care and sick-leave benefits, for example homemakers and the self-employed, even if National Insurance and employers pay more.
